goal: Roadmap R30: a per-repo reliability checklist whose items print only when the diff could repeat the mistake behind them, run by verify-work before a verdict and fed by correct.
changed: checklist.py --base REF reads .agents/checklist.json and prints the items whose trigger matches the diff, each with the file and line that fired it. It exits 0 when it ran and 2 when it could not.
The file format is JSON, chosen by a prototype: a regular expression with | breaks a Markdown table row unless a hand-written parser adds an escape rule.
agent-kit has its own checklist of five items: books layout, phase spec format, anything under plugins/, a gh call, a skill description.
verify-work runs the checklist before its verdict. correct sends a mistake a diff can show to the checklist instead of the rule table.
Short of the roadmap entry in one place: in a governed run each item is a hand-written verification ledger entry, not a receipt from receipt.py, which accepts only a phase spec criterion.

claims.claim: On agent-kit's history the checklist prints the books item and not the gh item at 990c84f, prints the gh item at 02faa18, and prints nothing on a docs-only commit (cb5299b).
claims.check: checklist.py --base C^ --head C for each commit, under /usr/bin/python3 3.9.6 on macOS
claims.remaining: Linux, and Python versions between 3.9 and 3.12.

claims.claim: The new checks fail on real past commits: the gh item fires on 74caa8d, the commit that introduced `gh auth status`, and the books item's probe fails at 990c84f on books written before it (exit 1) and passes on its own (exit 0).
claims.check: checklist.py --base 74caa8d^ --head 74caa8d; quality.py check from 990c84f on the fixture books of 990c84f^ and of 990c84f
claims.remaining: The probes of the other three items were not run against a past failure. Two of them (phase spec format, skill description) have no failure on record.

claims.claim: The script runs on every commit in the repo's history without an error.
claims.check: Replay over the 136 non-merge commits on origin/main that have a parent: 0 non-zero exits; 41 commits print nothing
claims.remaining: Whether each firing was useful. plugins-in-step fires on 95 of 136 commits, skill-description on 24, and books-layout on 9, most of them a new books file rather than a changed one.

claims.claim: Triggers match as documented: globs, added and removed lines, untracked files, --head. Every refusal exits 2 with a message, including a folder that is not the repo root, which is never read as a repo with no checklist.
claims.check: tests/test_checklist.py (24 tests on throwaway git repos) under /usr/bin/python3 3.9.6; make check validate unit (1,107 tests) under Python 3.12. With removed lines ignored on purpose, 2 of the tests fail.
claims.remaining: Linux, until this pull request's CI run finishes.

claims.claim: bstack 0.31.0 still installs into Claude Code, its skills load, and the what's-new hook shows the new entry.
claims.check: verify-kit: control-kit drive all, 4 of 4 features pass on the real claude CLI; make claude-validate passes
claims.remaining: A model choosing a skill from plain words, and tools other than Claude Code: verify-kit does not map them.

claims.claim: An agent following verify-work's new step runs the checklist and checks each item before its verdict.
claims.remaining: No eval ran on the changed skill text. The command in the step passes the command lint in make validate, and that is all.

next.item: agent-ledger's first checklist item: an entry format change keeps existing chains verifying
next.source: ROADMAP.md R30, last sentence of What
next.why_now: It needs this release installed, and it is one file in agent-ledger.
next.impact: A change to the ledger's entry format gets the question asked before merge. Left undone, only agent-kit has a checklist.

next.item: Decide what a receipt for a checklist item is
next.source: ROADMAP.md R30 ("in a governed run each item gets a receipt")
next.why_now: receipt.py refuses anything that is not a phase spec criterion, and its receipt shape belongs to agent-ledger's S3 spec. Extending either was out of scope here.
next.impact: Until then an item's result in a governed run is an entry an agent wrote by hand, which nothing checks against the probe's exit code.

next.item: Keep the checklist out of reach of the change it judges
next.why_now: The file is read from the working tree, so a pull request can delete the item that would have fired on it. R29's audit table should list it.
next.impact: A reviewer has to notice a diff to .agents/checklist.json. One fix: also read the base ref's copy and print items the diff removed or edited.
R40 adds its item to this checklist.
